pairs.subject: interview-run-of-show
pairs.evidence: app/api/interview-prep/importMerge.ts:85 The import merge only removes questions that match exactly after a trim, and only checks them against earlier imported entries. Near-duplicates, or questions already in the generated chronology, can pile up across re-imports, and the 40 cap is a payload-size limit, not the round's maximum question count.

techniques.evidence: app/api/interview-prep/importMerge.ts:85 The preserving half is realized: woven blockRefs survive a re-import, a no-op PATCH writes nothing (route.ts:283), and a staged pendingPlan gets accept/discard (route.ts:225). The technique's dedup rule is not met: matching is exact-string rather than normalised text, the comparison set is only importedQuestions and not the whole plan, and the cap (MAX_IMPORT_QUESTIONS=40, :8) guards payload size rather than the round's question count.

pairs.evidence: app/_lib/devcase-interview-kit.ts:27 The kit's question contract does tie each question to one observed decision, with listen-for and red-flag notes. It has no narrowing follow-up probe, no 'good answer contains' field, no gap bucket and no defence or weakest-point question, so the scaffold the technique requires is only partly carried.

techniques.evidence: app/_lib/devcase-interview-kit.ts:27 Grounding is realized: each question is anchored to one observed decision (header lines 2-4) and so is candidate-specific, not a topic list. Missing are the follow-up field, a bucket/defence question (the inverted weakest-point question for a clean record), and any cut to a round maximum: interviewKitMarkdown renders every usable question.

pairs.registryProposal: For a work-sample follow-up kit, every question has the same purpose: checking that the candidate authored a decision. That arguably makes it a single-bucket 'technical' kit. The technique could say whether a single-purpose kit still owes the bucket taxonomy, the catch-all and a defence question.
